claims.statement: The chat and embedding subsystems build on the cache subsystem: ChatModelProvider exposes its settings as a ChatCacheParameter and CachingChatModel/ChatModelUtils operate on Cache<ChatCacheKey>, while every real embedding creator receives a CacheManager and stores into Cache<EmbeddingCacheKey>; the cache backends read connection settings from a util-layer EnvironmentProvider, and the util layer depends on no internal packages.

Model settings travel as the framework-neutral records LlmConfiguration (platform, modelName, seed, temperature, environment) and EmbeddingConfiguration (platform, modelName, optional ONNX model/tokenizer paths, environment); platform endpoints are read from the environment (OLLAMA_HOST, OPENWEBUI_URL) or hardcoded per platform in ChatModelProvider, so nothing in the library depends on an application-specific configuration object.

Chat cache identity is ChatCacheParameter(modelName, seed, temperature) and every ChatCacheKey embeds model, seed, temperature, the CHAT mode, and the request content, so with a fixed seed and temperature identical requests are served from cache instead of being re-sent to the model (cost/latency reduction and reproducible runs); EmbeddingCacheKey pins seed and temperature to -1 and uses the EMBEDDING mode, so chat and embedding entries never collide and different models, seeds, and temperatures stay apart.

CachingChatModel implements caching once in doChat, the single point through which all ChatModel overloads are routed by the default interface methods: a cache hit returns the stored response without contacting the delegate; a miss delegates, caches the response text keyed by the string form of the messages, and flushes immediately so file-backed caches persist incrementally.

CachedEmbeddingCreator caches every embedding under a content-derived key, parallelizes batches with per-platform thread counts (OpenAI and Bifrost use 40 threads; Ollama, ONNX, and Open WebUI use 1), and recovers from over-long inputs by jtokkit-driven binary-search truncation to MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH 8000 whose result is cached under a separate _fixed_ key.

The no-global-environment invariant is enforced by two ArchUnit rules in NoGlobalEnvironmentTest over all non-test classes of edu.kit.kastel.mcse.ardoco.llm: no static field may have a type assignable to EnvironmentProvider, and CacheManager.getDefaultInstance() may be called only from EmbeddingCreator.create(EmbeddingConfiguration) — everywhere else the cache manager, and with it the cache environment, must be injected.

EmbeddingCreator.create(configuration) resolves the default CacheManager only for caching platforms: for the MOCK platform it returns a MockEmbeddingCreator (zero vectors of length 1, no cache, no environment reads) before the manager is touched, so a mock creator requires no cache setup.

Chat model creation is fail-fast but lazy: createChatModel() reads the required platform credentials eagerly from the configuration's environment (missing variables throw IllegalStateException before any model object exists, for every platform), while each platform branch returns a LazyChatModel that constructs the real LangChain4j client on first use via thread-safe double-checked locking.

CacheManager is the cache entry point: setCacheDir(dir[, environment]) must run before getDefaultInstance() (which throws IllegalStateException until then), getCache(origin, parameters) memoizes caches by sanitized name and rejects reuse with unequal parameters, builds the backend stack from CACHE_HIERARCHY (default LOCAL) folding multiple CacheTypes into HierarchicalCache with the CACHE_REPLACEMENT_STRATEGY (default NONE), and flush() persists every managed cache.

Each CacheManager holds the EnvironmentProvider it was created with, reads CACHE_HIERARCHY and CACHE_REPLACEMENT_STRATEGY from it at construction, and passes it to the Redis-based backends: RedisCache reads REDIS_URL (default redis://localhost:6379) and RestRedisCache reads REST_REDIS_URI with optional REST_REDIS_USERNAME/REST_REDIS_PASSWORD, both failing fast with IllegalStateException when the backend PING fails.

The LOCAL backend stores one self-contained JSON file per caller and model configuration named <Origin>_<model>_<seed>[_<temperature>].json (the temperature component is omitted when it is 0.0 for backward compatibility with LiSSA's existing caches), which makes a cache directory an offline replication package: layer LOCAL under REDIS/REST_REDIS while experimenting, flush at the end, ship the directory, and replicators re-run with CACHE_HIERARCHY=LOCAL without API keys or model access.

The library builds on Java 21 with the io.github.ardoco:parent 2.2.0-SNAPSHOT parent POM (artifact io.github.ardoco:llm-access, version 0.2.2-SNAPSHOT) and LangChain4j 1.23.0 imported as a BOM, using jtokkit 1.1.0 for token counting, org.fuchss:rest-redis 0.1.7 for the REST-Redis client, dotenv-java 3.2.0 for .env support, ArchUnit 1.5.1, and Testcontainers (2.0.5 BOM, test scope) for the Docker-gated integration test; flatten-maven-plugin is pinned to 1.9.0 because the ardoco parent references it unversioned and 1.8.0 has an NPE regression in its CI-friendly interpolator, and central-publishing overrides deploymentName to ardoco-llm-access with autoPublish and waitUntil published.

Both Redis-backed cache flavors operate behind the UnifiedRedisClient seam: RedisCache holds a UnifiedRedisClient backed by RedisAdapter (wrapping a Jedis UnifiedJedis), RestRedisCache extends RedisCache and connects through RestRedisAdapter (wrapping the org.fuchss rest-redis Client); both adapters implement the same ping/exists/hget/hset interface, and both connection setups fail fast with IllegalStateException when the server cannot be reached.

The Bifrost LLM gateway is a first-class platform for both chat and embeddings: ChatModelPlatform.BIFROST and EmbeddingPlatform.BIFROST route through the util-layer Bifrost helper, which reads the required BIFROST_URL and BIFROST_API_KEY variables (failing fast when either is missing) and sends the virtual key as bearer token plus the x-bf-vk header; model names are provider-prefixed, for example openai/gpt-4o-mini.

CacheManager.resetDefaultInstance() is package-private and exists solely for test isolation: it flushes the current default instance (if any) and clears it, so tests must call setCacheDir again before using the default instance; public consumers initialize the default instance via setCacheDir and getDefaultInstance.
